queue.name: Woodway Hyperscale Data Center Pipeline
queue.note: Woodway Energy Infrastructure signed agreements for a 22 mile, 30 inch line to a behind-the-meter power plant for an unnamed hyperscale data center, in service in the first half of 2028. No Woodway row exists. The state is not confirmed. RULING 10 RE-VET: last verdict (discovery-datacenter-recheck-20261019): monitor. Reason: no known state: the project is named by a sponsor with a public announcement, but the state is not disclosed, so the 'named project in a known state' leg of the data center add-threshold fails Notes: Woodway Energy Infrastructure announced on September 22, 2026 that it signed definitive agreements for a 22-mile, 30-inch natural gas pipeline. It will serve a power plant behind the meter for an unnamed hyperscale data center. Service is planned for the first half of 2028. Woodway describes itself as an owner of intrastate pipelines and is based in Houston. Press coverage points to Texas, but only as a guess from where Woodway's other assets are. The data center, the customer, the county and the state were not found in the press release, trade press, or search results. No existing row matches. Both sources are one press release reprinted, so they are not independent. Revisit when a state or county is named, for example in a Texas Railroad Commission filing. If it is added later: Owner Woodway Energy Infrastructure LLC (check entity lookup), 22 mi, 30 in, proposed, DataCenter yes, no route.

queue.name: Nexus Fulcrum Lateral
queue.note: A new lateral from the Great Basin system to a 510 MW gas plant meant to power data centers at the Tahoe Reno Industrial Center. Length and builder are unknown. The vetter must check whether it is the same as the industrial center spur already inside row P7860. RULING 10 RE-VET: last verdict (discovery-datacenter-recheck-20261019): monitor. Reason: No sponsor for the lateral itself is identified (the applicant is the plant developer, and the lateral builder is not confirmed), and it cannot be told apart from the Tahoe Reno Industrial Center end of the Great Basin 2028 Expansion (P7860). No length, route or filing for the pipe. Notes: A June 2026 New Project Media article says Nexus Fulcrum LLC applied on June 17 to the Public Utilities Commission of Nevada for a 510 MW gas plant at the former Fulcrum BioEnergy site in the Tahoe Reno Industrial Center, Storey County. It says gas would be supplied through a new lateral connecting to the Great Basin Pipeline system, and that the plant would serve one customer in the park and support expanded development there, including data centers. The article gives no length, route, owner or diameter for the lateral, and says the developer's link to Switch is unclear. The existing row P7860 (Great Basin 2028 Expansion) ends with a spur of about 14 miles into the same industrial center, where several gas plants are planned for November 2028. It is not known whether the plant lateral is that spur, a separate line, or a short in-fence connection, so a new row could duplicate P7860. No match was confirmed, so it is not classed as matched. Data center tie is through the plant (ruling 6) and would be tagged only once a source names the lateral's owner or filing. Re-check when the Nevada commission docket 26-06016 or a Great Basin filing names the lateral's builder and length.

queue.name: Stratos Project Ruby Pipeline Lateral
queue.note: Gas connection from the Ruby Pipeline (P0248) to the off-grid Stratos data center campus in Hansel Valley, Box Elder County, Utah. Length unknown. Ruby runs through the valley, so the connection may be very short. The Landgate piece calls on-site gas the original plan, so check whether it still stands. RULING 10 RE-VET: last verdict (discovery-datacenter-recheck-20261019): monitor. Reason: Stratos data center campus in Box Elder County, Utah plans gas from Ruby (P0248), and press says the Ruby could gain utilization. No named lateral, sponsor, length, route or signed gas deal found; the connection may be a short tap. Do not tag Ruby. Stays monitor; watch for a Tallgrass connection filing. Searches run: 8. Sources checked: Williams Socrates page, Ohio Power Siting Board coverage in Pipeline and Gas Journal, Natural Gas Intelligence, Data Center Dynamics, WyoFile, web searches.
